text:
maria: heads up — customer 'AtlasApps' reported CI deploys started failing around 08:12 UTC. lots of 401/403s from the deploy API. can someone look?

deploy-bot: Deploy job 987654 failed (atlasapps/prod) — exit code 1 — http 403 from /v1/deploy (job: ci/atlasapps-deploy/987654) :exclamation:

maria: pasted a snippet from the job logs:
```
+ curl -s -o /tmp/resp -w '%{http_code}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deploy
# output: 403
cat /tmp/resp
{"error":"insufficient_scope","required":["deploy:write"],"provided":["deploy:read"]}
```

sam: does this look like a scope regression? which token is the pipeline using (service account / token id)?

maria: the pipeline uses service account ci-deploy-bot@redwood. token id in the job logs: tok-9b3f2c. i'm not sure when it changed.

alex: audit-bot shows a token rotation event at 2026-03-15T08:05:12Z for ci-deploy-bot. audit snippet:
```
{"time":"2026-03-15T08:05:12Z","actor":"infra/sa-rotation","service_account":"ci-deploy-bot@redwood","token_id":"tok-9b3f2c","old_scopes":["deploy:write","deploy:read"],"new_scopes":["deploy:read"],"note":"rotation via sa-rotation job #2345"}
```

jen: that explains the insufficient_scope. the rotation job clipped deploy:write somehow. likely an infra config drift in the rotation template. quick repro: create a short-lived token from that SA with current template and call the deploy endpoint.

sam: trying a repro now (using a temporary token i created):
```
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer tok-9b3f2c" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deploy -i
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"insufficient_scope","required":["deploy:write"],"provided":["deploy:read"]}
```

sam: confirmed. we can either (A) fix the rotation template to include deploy:write for this SA, or (B) create a narrowly-scoped service account for deploys that explicitly has deploy:write and longer TTL. immediate mitigation: recreate a token that includes deploy:write and rotate pipelines to use it. longer-term: move pipelines to OIDC ephemeral creds.

maria: customer impact — blocked deploys for ~30 min so far. they asked about least-privilege; we should avoid giving broad org-level perms. prefer dedicated SA with minimal extra rights.

alex: opened an infra PR: https://git.company/infra/ops/merge_requests/412 — fixes the rotation template to preserve deploy:write for ci-deploy-bot and adds a test to prevent regressions. will also add a check that rotation jobs log the scopes they grant.

jen: action items:
- sam: rotate a temporary token with deploy:write and update the pipeline (hotfix) — set TTL 72h max.
- alex: merge PR to fix rotation template and add test.
- infra team: plan OIDC migration for atlasapps pipelines (ephemeral).

sam: hotfix applied — pipeline switched to token tok-9b3f5d which has deploy:write. re-ran job, deploy succeeded.

deploy-bot: Deploy job 987655 succeeded (atlasapps/prod) — http 200 — duration 43s :tada:

maria: thanks. can we also add a monitoring alert that detects when token rotations remove write scopes for SAs tagged as "ci-deploy"?

alex: yes — adding a scoped alert to the rotation monitor. my PR includes a small hook that emits a high-severity event when rotation removes previously-present write scopes for SA tags matching /ci-deploy/.

sam: long-term note in the thread: prefer OIDC for CI — no static tokens, and least privilege enforced by IAM role bindings. we'll create a migration playbook and share with customers.

maria: awesome. please post the links to the PR + playbook once ready. thanks all. :thumbsup:
